title: Policy-eval sandbox + lightweight authorization middleware for API/runtime/console
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an RBAC v2 policy evaluation sandbox and a lightweight authorization middleware that can be embedded into API gateway, runtime endpoints, and the Redwood Console. The goal is a low-latency fast-path for cached allow/deny decisions, an explainable evaluation path for audits, and improved SSO/SAML attribute mapping so console role syncs are deterministic. This ticket owns the core evaluator microservice, the middleware library for the runtime and console, and the audit context enrichment pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluator service exposes a gRPC and HTTP JSON endpoint with stable v1 API and schema
Middleware library (go/ts) returns allow/deny with decision_id within 4ms p95 on local benchmarks for cached decisions
Evaluator supports incremental delta evaluation for policy sets and exposes an explainable trace for each decision
Audit events include enriched context (actor_id, session_id, sso_provider, request_route, policy_snapshot_id) and are forwarded to the audit-collector with schema v2
SSO/SAML attribute mapping is pluggable and deterministic; Console role sync jobs show zero unexpected role deltas after mapping migration
End-to-end tests cover denial reason explanations, fallback to deny-by-default, and deterministic rollout behavior for canary policies
tasks: Design policy sandbox controller that can load multiple policy bundles for safe evaluation
Implement evaluator with WASM-backed rule execution for isolation and speed
Add explainability layer: decision_id -> evaluation_steps -> matched_rules list
Create go middleware for runtime and a TS middleware for Console that use local cache + remote evaluator fallback
Implement audit context enricher and schema v2 mapping in audit-collector
Write SSO attribute mapping adapter and migration script for Console role sync
Performance test harness and p95/p99 goals verification
End-to-end regression tests and canary rollout plan
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Spiked a WASM approach in branch feature/wasm-eval. Initial numbers show sub-2ms for very small rulesets, but cold startup of WASM instances is ~12ms. Need warm-pool strategy.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Proposal to use a tiny local LRU cache keyed by (actor, route, resource, policy_snapshot_id) to hit fast-path. Cache invalidation will be driven by policy_snapshot_id TTLs and explicit invalidation events from the policy-store stream.

2026-03-12 PM review (Riley Morgan): Confirmed customer requirements for explainability and audit enrichment. Suggested adding a field in audit events for 'decision_human_summary' for compliance reviewers.
2026-03-12 Security (Marta Alvarez): Requested threat model review for WASM policy execution and KMS usage for signing policy snapshots. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-13 Design (Evan Brooks): Console UX note: show 'last evaluated at' and a concise reason string for denied actions. Will provide mockups in design doc link below.

2026-03-14 Liam Chen: Implemented initial middleware prototype in go: pkg/authz/middleware with metrics and traces. Pushed PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8453 - awaiting code review. Added unit tests for deny-by-default behavior.
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Chose WASM for policy execution to get strong isolation and language-agnostic rule runtimes. Agreed to mitigate cold-start via warm pools and prefetching.
2026-03-12: Fast-path cache will be conservative and only return cached ALLOW if policy_snapshot_id matches; otherwise fallback to remote evaluator to avoid stale allow decisions.
2026-03-13: Audit events will include a 'policy_snapshot_id' and a cryptographic signature (policy_snapshot_sig) to enable off-line verification of decision inputs during compliance audits.

2026-03-14: Will implement SSO mapping as pluggable adapters; default adapter maps SAML 'roles' claim to internal role IDs with a deterministic sort-and-hash step to avoid nondeterministic maps across runs.
notes: Trade-offs: WASM gives isolation but requires warm pools; alternative was embedding a native evaluator but that increases blast radius. We prefer explainability and auditable inputs even if the fast-path cache reduces some evaluation frequency. Next steps: finalize schema v1 for evaluator API, implement migration script for Console role sync, and complete PR review for middleware.
